# **TNFS (PlayStation) file specs** #

*Last time updated: 2026-10-20 12:50:27.906335+00:00*

*Generated by [TailsLab](../README.md) from its parser code.*


# **Info by file extensions** #

File names on the disc (SLUS-00204) are upper case. Most files end with a CRC footer: [PsxCrcFooter](#psxcrcfooter)

**\*.PSH** image archive. [ShppBlock](#shppblock). `Z<track><A|B|C>.PSH` are the textures of a track at a time of day (A morning, B midday, C evening), with the horizon images `hrz0`..`hrz7` and `rhrz`; `ZG*.PSH` are German versions of some files. The converter writes the sky sphere texture `spherical.png` next to the PNGs of a track's textures, from the horizon images and the `.INF` file of the same name

**\*.INF** horizon settings of a track at a time of day, plain text. [TnfsPsxHorizonInfo](#tnfspsxhorizoninfo)

**Z<track>_PSH.FAM** [WwwwBlock](#wwwwblock) of [ShppBlock](#shppblock) items. The CRC footer follows its last item

Did not find what you need or some given data is wrong? Please submit an
[issue](https://github.com/AndyGura/nfs-resources-converter/issues/new)


# **Block specs** #
## **Archives** ##
### **ShppBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A container of PSX images (`.PSH` files of the PSX TNFS, also inside its `_PSH.FAM` wwww archives): the PSX counterpart of SHPI, same header and directory. The game finds an image by its 4-character name (`tnfs_front_image` 0x80010334, case-sensitive). Track textures `Z<track><time>.PSH` hold the horizon: `hrz0`..`hrz7` (8 sectors of 22.5 degrees each) and `rhrz` (rear-view mirror) ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "SHPP" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | The length of this SHPP block in bytes, without the CRC footer of the file |
| 8 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of items |
| 12 | **shpi_dir** | 4 | UTF-8 string | Directory id: "GIMX" in every file |
| 16 | **items_descr** | num_items\*8 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 8 bytes<br/>Item type: 8-bytes record, first 4 bytes is a UTF-8 string, last 4 bytes is an unsigned integer (little-endian) | An array of items, each of them represents name of SHPI item (image or palette) and offset to item data in file, relatively to SHPI block start (where resource id string is presented). Names are not always unique |
| 16 + num_items\*8 | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 16 + num_items\*8 + up to the first item offset | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets to the entries are defined in `items_descr`. Every item is padded to 4 bytes. Possible item types:<br/>- [PsxImage](#psximage) |
| 16 + num_items\*8 + up to the first item offset + up to end of block | **crc_footer** | 0..12 | Optional (if at least 1 byte remaining): [PsxCrcFooter](#psxcrcfooter) | CRC footer after the SHPP (`length` does not count it), in a file of its own only: inside a FAM archive it follows the last item of the FAM |
### **WwwwBlock** ###
#### **Size**: 8..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: A block-container with various data: image archives, geometries, other wwww blocks. If has ORIP 3D model, next item is always SHPI block with textures to this 3D model ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "wwww" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **num_items** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An amount of items |
| 8 | **items_descr** | num_items\*4 | Array of `num_items` items<br/>Item size: 4 bytes<br/>Item type: 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | An array of offsets to items data in file, relatively to wwww block start (where resource id string is presented) |
| 8 + num_items\*4 | **pre_items_payload** | up to the first item offset | Bytes | Bytes between the end of `items_descr` and the first item: padding, or data which no item offset points to |
| 8 + num_items\*4 + up to the first item offset | **data_bytes** | up to end of block | Bytes | A part of block, where items data is located. Offsets are defined in previous block, lengths are calculated: either up to next item offset, or up to the end of this block. Possible item types:<br/>- [ShppBlock](#shppblock)<br/>- [WwwwBlock](#wwwwblock) |
## **Images** ##
### **PsxImage** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: An image of a PSX SHPP archive: 4-bit or 8-bit indexed with its CLUT, or 16-bit PSX colors. The rows are stored as uploaded to VRAM (whole 16-bit words, 4-bit pixels low nibble first). An image with the rotated flag in `vram_x` is stored rotated by 90 degrees: the game maps it so that it shows `height` texels wide and `width` texels high (stored left column, bottom to top = shown top row, left to right). The converter exports images as they are shown ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | Enum of 256 possible values<br/><details><summary>Value names:</summary>64 (0x40): 4Bit PSX<br/>65 (0x41): 8Bit PSX<br/>66 (0x42): 16Bit PSX</details> | Resource ID: its low 2 bits are the PSX texture color mode the loader uses (0 4-bit, 1 8-bit, 2 16-bit) |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset from the start of the image to its CLUT (4-bit and 8-bit images), 0 when nothing is attached (16-bit images). Recomputed on save |
| 4 | **width** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Width in pixels, as stored (shown height when rotated) |
| 6 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Height in pixels, as stored (shown width when rotated) |
| 8 | **pivot** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes signed integer (little endian) | At the place of the SHPI `pivot`. 0 in track textures; front end images and the rear-view mirror horizon `rhrz` have values. Not read by the horizon code, purpose not verified |
| 12 | **vram_x** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bits 0-13: x of the image in VRAM in 16-bit words, where the tool that made the file packed it (the loader uploads it there, FUN_800b5628; the UVs are its offset in the 64-word texture page). Bit 14: the image is stored rotated (FUN_80044330 swaps its UVs) |
| 14 | **vram_y** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Bits 0-13: y of the image in VRAM. Bit 14 is set together with the rotated bit of `vram_x`, the loader does not read it |
| 16 | **bitmap** | height \* ceil(width \* bits_per_pixel / 16) \* 2 | Bytes | Pixels, row by row, each row padded to whole 16-bit words: CLUT indexes (4-bit: the first pixel in the low nibble) or PSX 16-bit colors (bits 0-4 red, 5-9 green, 10-14 blue, 15 STP). 0x0000 colors are transparent. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md) |
| 16 + height \* ceil(width \* bits_per_pixel / 16) \* 2 | **pad** | up to `next_offset` | Bytes | Zeros aligning the CLUT to 4 bytes (images with an odd amount of 16-bit words) |
| 16 + height \* ceil(width \* bits_per_pixel / 16) \* 2 + up to `next_offset` | **clut** | 0..? | Optional (if `next_offset` points to a CLUT (0x23)): [PsxClut](#psxclut) | The CLUT of a 4-bit or 8-bit image |
### **PsxClut** ###
#### **Size**: 16..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: CLUT (color look-up table) of a PSX 4-bit or 8-bit image, attached to it (the image `next_offset` points to it). The colors are PSX 16-bit colors: bits 0-4 red, 5-9 green, 10-14 blue, 15 STP (semi-transparency). 0x0000 is transparent: the GPU does not draw such texels ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 1 | 1-byte unsigned integer. Always == 0x23 | Resource ID |
| 1 | **next_offset** | 3 | 3-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Offset to the next block attached to the image: 0 in every file, the CLUT is the last |
| 4 | **num_colors** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Amount of colors (the width of the CLUT in VRAM): 16 for 4-bit images, 256 for 8-bit ones (a few 8-bit images use only 16 or 64) |
| 6 | **height** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Rows of colors: 1 in every file |
| 8 | **num_colors_2** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | Equals `num_colors` |
| 10 | **unk** | 2 | 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | 0 in every file |
| 12 | **vram_position** | 4 | Point in 2D space (x,y), where each coordinate is: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | VRAM position (0, 240 in every file). The game does not use it: the loader puts the CLUT in a free VRAM slot (FUN_80044794) |
| 16 | **colors** | num_colors\*height\*2 | Array of `num_colors*height` items<br/>Item size: 2 bytes<br/>Item type: 2-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | PSX 16-bit colors. Color models are described [here](eac_colors.md) |
## **Misc** ##
### **TnfsPsxHorizonInfo** ###
#### **Size**: 0..? bytes ####
#### **Description**: Horizon settings of a PSX TNFS track at a time of day, `Z<track><A|B|C>.INF` (A morning, B midday, C evening), the counterpart of the PC `SIMDATA/MISC/<track>INFO`. Plain text: `#` comment lines, then one value per line (colors: 3 on a line). Read by FUN_80034adc in this order: 8 ring geometry values (vert offset near / far, z offset near / far, height near / far, radius near / far; the ring points are at radius far around the camera, at height vert offset far and z offset far, 0 in every file; a horizon is drawn only when height far is not 0, 48 in every file), colour top and colour bottom (RGB 0..255), dithering flag (GPU dithering of the sky gradient), ratio of the blend, ring y offset, ring height (both halved by the game: px of the 320x240 screen; the PC uses them as px of 640x480), and a last value without a comment, the mirror flag (sectors 8..15 of the ring show `hrz7`..`hrz0` mirrored). Unlike the PC there is no ring type (the PSX always draws the ring) and no time of day values. See `library/utils/tnfs_psx_horizon_to_spherical.py` for how the game draws them ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **text** | up to the CRCF footer | UTF-8 string | The settings text |
| up to the CRCF footer | **crc_footer** | 0..12 | Optional (if the file ends with "CRCF"): [PsxCrcFooter](#psxcrcfooter) | CRC footer |
### **PsxCrcFooter** ###
#### **Size**: 12 bytes ####
#### **Description**: Footer of most PSX TNFS files (PSH, INF, LGT, LGS, TRI, FAM, VB, VH, PFN...): the file loader FUN_8001577c checks it (callback 0x80015958: FUN_80015858 finds the footer, FUN_800158d4 compares the CRC) and loads the file again when it does not match. Inside a FAM (wwww) archive it follows the last item, in the bytes after it ####
| Offset | Name | Size (bytes) | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 0 | **resource_id** | 4 | UTF-8 string. Always == "CRCF" | Resource ID |
| 4 | **length** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian). Always == 0xc | Footer length |
| 8 | **crc** | 4 | 4-bytes unsigned integer (little endian) | CRC-16 of every byte of the file before the footer: reflected, polynomial 0x8005, initial value 0xFBEA, no final xor (PSX `math_func_010` 0x800b4850). Recomputed on save |
